questions.questionText: A farmer plants 4 hectares at a seed rate of 12 kg/ha. What quantity of seed is required?
questions.explanation: Seed required = area × seed rate = 4 × 12 = 48 kg.

questions.questionText: A farmer obtains a soil pH of 6. Which amendment would generally be used to raise the pH of an acidic soil?
questions.explanation: Agricultural lime neutralises soil acidity and raises soil pH.

questions.questionText: Which operation should normally be carried out after sowing a crop when the main aim is to reduce competition from unwanted plants?
questions.explanation: Weeding removes or suppresses weeds so that the crop has less competition for light, water and nutrients.

questions.questionText: Which method is most appropriate for reducing the spread of a seed-borne fungal disease before planting?
questions.explanation: Certified treated seed reduces the risk of introducing seed-borne pathogens into the field.

questions.questionText: Which feature is most useful when selecting cattle for a beef-production enterprise?

options.text: Good growth rate and feed conversion

questions.explanation: Beef cattle are selected for desirable growth, carcass and feed-utilisation traits.

questions.questionText: Which nutrient is primarily required by livestock for body building, tissue repair and production of enzymes?
questions.explanation: Protein supplies amino acids needed for growth, tissue repair and many metabolic functions.

questions.questionText: Which observation would most strongly suggest that an animal requires veterinary attention?

options.text: Persistent loss of appetite and abnormal behaviour

questions.explanation: Persistent loss of appetite together with abnormal behaviour can indicate illness and warrants examination.

questions.questionText: Why are legumes valuable components of many pastures?

options.text: They can fix atmospheric nitrogen through symbiotic bacteria

questions.explanation: Legumes form symbiotic associations with nitrogen-fixing bacteria, improving nitrogen availability in the pasture.

questions.questionText: Which farm tool is primarily used for loosening soil and making planting holes on a small holding?
questions.explanation: A hoe is a common hand tool for loosening soil, making planting holes and controlling weeds.

questions.questionText: If total variable costs rise while output price and output remain unchanged, what happens to gross margin?
questions.explanation: Gross margin equals gross income minus variable costs, so higher variable costs reduce gross margin when other factors stay constant.

questions.questionText: Which record is most useful for determining the quantities of fertiliser purchased and used on a farm?
questions.explanation: An input record documents purchases and use of inputs such as fertiliser, seed and chemicals.

questions.questionText: Which practice is most effective for reducing soil erosion on sloping cultivated land?

options.text: Cultivating up and down the slope

questions.explanation: Contour cultivation slows runoff across slopes and helps reduce soil erosion.

questions.questionText: Which weather instrument is used to measure rainfall?
questions.explanation: A rain gauge measures the amount of precipitation received over a specified period.

questions.questionText: Which propagation method produces a new plant from a vegetative part of the parent plant rather than from a seed?
questions.explanation: A stem cutting is a vegetative propagation method in which a stem section develops roots and shoots.

questions.questionText: Which farm-management practice is most appropriate when a farmer wants to compare the performance of two enterprises using their costs and returns?
questions.explanation: Gross-margin analysis compares enterprise variable costs and returns and is used to support farm-management decisions.

questions.questionText: Which marketing function involves collecting produce from several farmers and assembling it into larger quantities for buyers?
questions.explanation: Bulking combines produce into larger marketable quantities.

questions.questionText: Which Zimbabwean agro-ecological natural region receives the highest annual rainfall (>1,000 mm) and specialises in tea, coffee, timber, and intensive dairy farming?
questions.explanation: Natural Region I (Eastern Highlands) receives >1,000 mm rainfall per year.

questions.questionText: Which soil horizon is richest in organic humus and dark minerals essential for shallow crop roots?
questions.explanation: Topsoil (Horizon A) contains decomposed organic matter, microbes, and available nutrients.

questions.questionText: Which mineral nutrient deficiency in maize causes purple discolouration along lower leaves and weak root establishment?
questions.explanation: Phosphorus deficiency leads to purpling of leaves and stunted root systems.

questions.questionText: Which crop pest attacks maize stems by boring inside the stalk and damaging the growing point ("dead heart")?
questions.explanation: Stalk borer larvae tunnel down the maize funnel and stem.

questions.questionText: In ruminant cattle digestion, where does microbial fermentation of cellulose fibre primarily occur?
questions.explanation: The large rumen houses symbiotic bacteria and protozoa that ferment cellulose.

questions.questionText: Which tick-borne cattle disease in Zimbabwe is caused by Theileria parva and often causes swollen lymph nodes and high fever?
questions.explanation: January disease (Theileriosis) is transmitted by brown ear ticks, especially in wet summer months.

questions.questionText: What is the main function of the mouldboard on an ox-drawn mouldboard plough?

options.text: Inverts the cut furrow slice to bury weeds and crop residues

questions.explanation: The curved mouldboard turns over the soil slice cut by the share.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a variable cost in maize production?

options.text: Hybrid seed and ammonium nitrate fertiliser

questions.explanation: Variable costs change directly with the scale of planting/production (seed, fertiliser, casual labour).

questions.questionText: Why are groundnuts or soya beans planted before maize in a crop rotation?

options.text: Their root-nodule Rhizobium bacteria fix atmospheric nitrogen into nitrates
They eliminate the need for rain

questions.explanation: Legumes host Rhizobium bacteria in root nodules that enrich soil nitrogen for subsequent maize.

questions.questionText: What does "carrying capacity" of a pasture mean?

options.text: Maximum weight a farm trailer can haul
Maximum number of livestock units a grazing area can support without pasture degradation
Total water volume of a borehole

questions.explanation: Carrying capacity balances stocking rate against sustainable grass regeneration.

questions.questionText: Which irrigation method delivers water drop by drop directly at plant roots with minimal evaporation loss?
questions.explanation: Drip irrigation achieves the highest water-use efficiency in dry regions.

questions.questionText: Which poultry disease causes twisted necks, greenish diarrhoea, and sudden high flock mortality, controlled by routine vaccination?
questions.explanation: Newcastle disease is a notifiable viral killer prevented through live vaccination programmes.

questions.questionText: In farm fencing, what is the purpose of a corner/strainer post with diagonal stays?

options.text: To absorb high pulling tension when straining barbed wire

questions.explanation: Braced strainer posts anchor wire tension along fence lines without leaning.

questions.questionText: Which herbicide type kills only targeted broadleaf weeds while leaving narrow-leaved maize unharmed?
questions.explanation: Selective herbicides target specific weed families without killing the crop.

questions.questionText: Which livestock management practice involves removing horn buds from young calves (1–2 weeks old) using a hot iron?
questions.explanation: Disbudding prevents adult cattle injuring each other or workers in pens.

questions.questionText: Why should top-dressing fertiliser (AN) be applied as split applications on sandy soils?

options.text: Because sandy soil has high clay content
To reduce nitrate leaching loss during heavy rainstorms

questions.explanation: Split dressing matches maize uptake and reduces nitrogen washing below the root zone.

questions.questionText: What is the ideal moisture content for safe long-term storage of shelled maize grain in silos?
questions.explanation: Drying grain to ≤12% moisture prevents fungal mould and aflatoxin growth.

questions.questionText: Which forest tree genus widely grown in Zimbabwe's Eastern Highlands provides fast-growing poles and firewood?
questions.explanation: Eucalyptus plantations supply timber, treated poles, and fuelwood rapidly.

questions.questionText: In Mendelian genetics used in livestock breeding, what is a cross between two unrelated pure breeds called?
questions.explanation: Crossbreeding combines desirable traits from two breeds to achieve heterosis (hybrid vigour).

questions.questionText: Which government agency in Zimbabwe buys and maintains strategic national maize grain reserves?
questions.explanation: The Grain Marketing Board (GMB) handles strategic grain purchasing and storage.
